items.title: Three charged over arson attack on Jewish ambulances in London

featured_image.name: Three more people arrested in Golders Green ambulance attack ...

items.description: British prosecutors have charged three people following the arson attack that destroyed four Jewish volunteer ambulances in Golders Green, north London, on March 23. Hamza Iqbal, 20, and Rehan Khan, 19, both British nationals from Leyton in east London, along with a 17-year-old boy — a dual British and Pakistani national from Walthamstow — each face a charge of arson being reckless as to whether life would be endangered. The three are set to appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Saturday, April 4.[1][2][3]

items.title: Earthquake kills 8 in Afghanistan, tremors felt across South Asia

featured_image.name: Eight dead after earthquake of magnitude 5.9 strikes ...

items.description:
A magnitude 5.9 earthquake struck Afghanistan's Hindu Kush region on Friday, killing at least eight people when a house collapsed on the outskirts of Kabul, authorities said.

The victims were all members of the same family, according to Hafizullah Basharat, a spokesman for the Kabul governor, who said a child was also injured in the collapse in the capital's Bagrami district. Afghanistan's National Disaster Management Authority confirmed the casualties.[1][2]

items.title: Zelenskyy accuses Russia of 'Easter escalation' after massive daytime strike kills six

featured_image.name: Zelensky accuses Russia of 'buying time' to stall truce talks

items.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Friday accused Russia of an "Easter escalation" after Moscow launched nearly 500 drones and cruise missiles at Ukrainian cities in broad daylight, killing at least six people, even as the two sides negotiate a prisoner-of-war exchange ahead of Orthodox Easter on April 12.

items.title: US intel finds Iran unlikely to negotiate on Hormuz blockade

featured_image.name: How US-Israel attacks on Iran threaten the Strait of Hormuz, oil ...

items.description:
Multiple U.S. intelligence agencies have concluded that Iran is not inclined to enter serious negotiations to end its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, according to officials familiar with the assessments, dimming hopes for a near-term reopening of the world's most critical energy chokepoint and keeping global oil markets on edge.[1]

The assessments, reported by The New York Times, indicate that Tehran perceives itself as being in a strong position and sees no need to comply with American demands, even as the conflict enters its sixth week. The intelligence findings land as President Trump's April 6 deadline for Iran to reopen the strait draws near, with no clear diplomatic pathway in sight.[2][3][1]

items.title: War silences Good Friday in Jerusalem as Pope Leo XIV calls for peace

featured_image.name: Christians mark subdued Good Friday in Jerusalem, wider ...

items.description: Only a handful of worshippers walked the Via Dolorosa in Jerusalem's Old City on Friday, as Israeli security restrictions sharply limited access to Christianity's holiest sites during one of the faith's most solemn days. The traditional Good Friday procession, which normally draws thousands of pilgrims retracing the path of Jesus to his crucifixion, was cancelled this year due to the ongoing war between the United States, Israel, and Iran.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Russia holds nuclear missile drills as Trump threatens NATO exit

featured_image.name: Russian nuclear missile forces undergo drills in Siberia ...

items.description: Russia's strategic missile forces conducted large-scale exercises in Siberia involving Yars intercontinental ballistic missiles on Friday, the Russian Defence Ministry announced, in a show of nuclear readiness that coincided with a deepening rift between the United States and its NATO allies over President Donald Trump's threat to leave the alliance.[1][2]

items.title: Qatar rebuffs lead mediator role in US-Iran ceasefire talks

featured_image.name: Qatar's foreign ministry says drafts of possible agreement sent to both  Hamas and Israel | Reuters

items.description: Qatar has pushed back against efforts by the United States and regional nations to assume a central role in mediating a potential ceasefire with Iran, dealing a fresh blow to diplomatic efforts to end the monthlong war, according to The Wall Street Journal. Gulf officials told U.S. representatives last week that Doha was not interested in leading the mediation process, the Journal reported Friday.[1]

items.title: Iran rejects US 48-hour ceasefire proposal as Hormuz deadline nears

featured_image.name: Tehran rejected 48-hour ceasefire proposal from US, Iranian ...

items.description: Iran has rejected a US proposal for a 48-hour ceasefire, an unnamed source told the country's semi-official Fars news agency on Friday, dealing a fresh blow to diplomatic efforts to end a war now in its sixth week. The proposal was conveyed on Wednesday through an unidentified intermediary country, according to Reuters, and there was no immediate comment from the US.[1][2]

items.title: Israel pounds Beirut as US warns of Iran threat to universities

featured_image.name: Israel strikes Beirut, US warns Iran may hit Lebanese universities | Reuters

items.description:
Israel pounded Beirut with airstrikes on Friday targeting what its military described as militant "infrastructure" in Lebanon's capital, according to Reuters, as the five-week-old war between Israel and Hezbollah continued to escalate. The strikes hit the southern suburbs of Beirut, an area largely controlled by Hezbollah that has been the focus of repeated Israeli bombardment since hostilities reignited in early March.[1][2][3]

The Israeli military issued evacuation warnings to residents ahead of the strikes, a pattern that has become routine throughout the conflict. The strikes followed days of intensifying Israeli operations across Lebanon, including a Wednesday attack on Beirut's Jnah district that killed at least five people and wounded 21, and a separate strike in Khaldeh that killed two more, according to Lebanon's health ministry.[4][5][6][7]

items.title: Israel launches airstrikes on Tehran and Beirut simultaneously

featured_image.name: Iran's Revolutionary Guard threatens US universities in the Middle ...

items.description:
Israel launched airstrikes on both Beirut and Tehran on Friday, opening a new front of simultaneous attacks as the broader U.S.-Israeli war against Iran entered its 34th day. Reuters reporters in Beirut heard three loud blasts echoing across the city around sunset on Good Friday, as many of Lebanon's Christians marked the solemn holiday. The Israel Defense Forces separately announced it had begun an "extensive" wave of strikes targeting Iranian regime infrastructure in the capital Tehran.[1][2]

The IDF said the Beirut strikes targeted what it described as "terror infrastructure" in the city's southern suburbs, a Hezbollah stronghold that has been battered repeatedly since the conflict with the Iran-backed group reignited in early March. The strikes in Tehran were concurrent with the Beirut operations, according to the Israeli military, which did not initially provide further details on the Iranian targets. The IDF said over the previous 24 hours it had struck more than 70 Iranian missile and drone arrays across the country.[3][1]

items.title: Pilot rescued after US A-10 Warthog crashes near Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: U.S. Air Force to retire A-10 attack aircraft in South Korea by fiscal year  2025 | Reuters

items.description: A U.S. Air Force A-10 Thunderbolt II crashed near the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, with its sole pilot safely rescued, according to The New York Times, citing two U.S. officials who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss operational matters. The incident marked the second American combat aircraft lost in a single day during Operation Epic Fury, occurring around the same time an F-15E Strike Eagle was shot down over Iran.[1][2]

items.title: Iran claims second US F-35 downed as Pentagon denies loss

featured_image.name: Iran shares photos of F-35 wreckage; analysts say images ...

items.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said Friday that it shot down a US F-35 stealth fighter jet over Markazi province in central Iran, the second such claim in 24 hours as the war between the United States, Israel, and Iran enters its fifth week. The Pentagon has not confirmed the claim, and US Central Command posted on social media that "all U.S. fighter aircraft are accounted for," adding that Iran's IRGC "has made the same false claim at least half a dozen times".[1]

items.title: UN delays Hormuz vote to Saturday after stripping military enforcement powers

featured_image.name: UN proposal on opening Strait of Hormuz gets watered down

items.description:
India finds itself at the center of one of the most consequential diplomatic standoffs of the Gulf conflict, threading a needle between its Western partners, its BRICS allies, and its own energy security interests as the United Nations Security Council prepares to vote on a Bahrain-drafted resolution to protect shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

The vote, initially expected Friday, has been pushed to Saturday due to the Good Friday holiday at the UN. The final text, now stripped of its original Chapter VII enforcement authority after six successive drafts over 15 days, authorizes member states to use "all defensive means necessary and commensurate with the circumstances" to secure passage through the strait — but explicitly rules out offensive military action.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: UN delays vote on Hormuz shipping resolution to Saturday

featured_image.name: Bahrain waters down UN proposal over opposition to allowing force to open  Strait of Hormuz

items.description:
The United Nations Security Council on Friday postponed a vote on a Bahrain-led draft resolution that would authorize the use of "defensive" force to protect commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, with diplomats indicating a new vote could take place as early as Saturday, April 4.[1][2][3]

The vote had been scheduled for Friday morning but was pushed back on the grounds that the UN observes Good Friday as a public holiday — a fact that was already known when the vote was initially planned. Some diplomatic sources said no firm new date had been set, though Reuters and other outlets reported Saturday as the likely target.[3][4][5][1]

items.title: UN says Iran war is accelerating global renewable energy shift

featured_image.name: Iran war: A global energy shock could accelerate a shift to renewables

items.description: The month-old U.S.-Israeli war with Iran has triggered the largest oil supply disruption in history, and analysts say the crisis is now accelerating a global pivot toward renewable energy as countries scramble to reduce their dependence on fossil fuels funneled through vulnerable chokepoints.

items.title: Macron calls for 'coalition of independence' against US and China

featured_image.name: Macron Urges Countries To Stand Up To 'Hegemonic Powers' U.S. ...

items.description:
French President Emmanuel Macron on Friday urged democratic nations to form a "coalition of independence" to resist the dominance of both the United States and China, delivering a pointed address to students at Yonsei University in Seoul during his first visit to South Korea in over a decade.

"Our objective is not to be the vassals of two hegemonic powers," Macron said, warning countries against falling under China's "dominance" while also shielding themselves from what he called the "unpredictability" of the United States. He proposed an alliance of middle powers including European nations, Japan, South Korea, Brazil, Canada, and India — countries he said share commitments to democracy and international law.[1][2]

items.title: U.S. F-15E shot down over Iran; one crew member rescued

featured_image.name: U.S. Denies F-15E Strike Eagle Went Down In Iran - Yahoo

items.description: A U.S. Air Force F-15E Strike Eagle was shot down over southwestern Iran on Friday, and one of its two crew members has been rescued by American forces, according to U.S. officials cited by The Wall Street Journal and CBS News. The loss marks the first confirmed shootdown of a manned American combat aircraft by enemy fire since the U.S.-Iran war began on February 28.[1][2][3]

items.title: IDF says disarming Hezbollah 'not a goal' of Lebanon campaign

featured_image.name: Israel planning massive ground invasion of Lebanon, officials say

items.description:
The Israeli military said Friday that it has struck more than 3,500 targets across Lebanon in the month since fighting with Hezbollah erupted on March 2, a figure that underscores the scale of Israel's air and ground campaign against the Iran-backed militia.[1][2]

The targets include weapons depots, rocket and missile launch sites, command centers, and anti-tank missile positions, according to the IDF. The military also said it has killed approximately 1,000 Hezbollah operatives since hostilities began, including hundreds of members of the group's elite Radwan Force.[3][2][1]

items.title: Trump says Israel will halt Iran war on his orders

featured_image.name: Trump Promises Iran War Is 'Nearing Completion' - TIME

items.description:
President Donald Trump declared that Israel would halt its military campaign against Iran on his orders, asserting his personal authority over the course of the five-week-old conflict in an interview with TIME magazine published on Thursday.

"They'll do what I tell them," Trump said of the Israelis. "They've been a good team player. They'll stop when I stop. They'll stop unless they're provoked, in which case, they'll have no choice, but they'll stop when I stop."[1][2]

The remarks, made in a phone call with TIME on the morning of April 2, came hours after Trump threatened further escalation in the war in a post on Truth Social. "Our Military… hasn't even started destroying what's left in Iran. Bridges next, then Electric Power Plants!" he wrote, adding that Iran's "New Regime leadership knows what has to be done, and has to be done, FAST!"[3][4]

items.title: Artemis II crew shares first photos of Earth from deep space

featured_image.name: NASA releases pictures of earth from Artemis II

items.description: NASA released the first images downlinked from the Artemis II astronauts on Friday, revealing Earth in vivid detail as the crew races toward the Moon on the first human lunar voyage in more than half a century.
